samples.claim: Public has_writer_placed_lineage returns true iff row_id_meta is Column OR created_at_version_meta is Column. A last_updated_at Column alone does not qualify. It does not check physical count, carrier files, flags, provenance or payload validity. Docs explain trusting writer-placed creation lineage while recomputing inline/inline creation lineage; the doctest changes an empty Fragment to row-ID Column and asserts classification. Actual output validation/stamping is separate; this predicate is publicly callable through the transaction reexport.
samples.evidence:
54 | /// Whether an update's new `fragment` carries row lineage its writer placed
55 | /// outside the manifest, which the commit keeps instead of resolving.
56 | ///
57 | /// That is spilled row ids or spilled created-at versions. The commit cannot
58 | /// read either back, and only a writer carrying the lineage of rows it read
59 | /// over into the fragment produces them. Inline created-at versions next to
60 | /// inline row ids do not count: the commit resolves those again from the row
61 | /// ids, whatever the caller supplied, so a hand-built transaction cannot
62 | /// commit stale ones.
63 | ///
64 | /// ```
65 | /// use lance_table::format::{Fragment, RowIdMeta};
66 | /// use lance_table::transaction::has_writer_placed_lineage;
67 | ///
68 | /// let mut fragment = Fragment::new(0);
69 | /// assert!(!has_writer_placed_lineage(&fragment));
70 | /// fragment.row_id_meta = Some(RowIdMeta::Column);
71 | /// assert!(has_writer_placed_lineage(&fragment));
72 | /// ```
73 | pub fn has_writer_placed_lineage(fragment: &Fragment) -> bool {
74 |     matches!(fragment.row_id_meta, Some(RowIdMeta::Column))
75 |         || matches!(
76 |             fragment.created_at_version_meta,
77 |             Some(RowDatasetVersionMeta::Column)
78 |         )
79 | }
80 |
samples.review_note: Exact OR of row-ID Column and created-at Column, doctest and reexport route match.

Overlays have default empty serde and skip when empty; deletion/lineage options skip when None, while physical_rows remains serialized even when unknown. Overlay order is significant, later newer by contract; serde itself does not normalize it.

samples.claim: Require every original fragment ID in the stored bitmap; empty originals pass vacuously and u64 IDs cast to u32 unchecked.
